decisions.summary: The first house is offered the free ground nearest the seat point (capacity.free_seats through the seat region, at most DRY_SPELL offers) until one stands
decisions.why: US1 puts the first house at the cluster's seed point and FR-006 lets the placer decide; offering the nearest lawful ground to that point is that, for one house only. It is not FR-007's exhaustive pass, which seats the quota.

decisions.summary: Every standing house offers seats in a ring of directions jittered positionally (+/-12 deg, up to +12% distance) at the distance where the two footprints part plus GROW_GAP
decisions.why: FR-004 as written: from a standing house, direction and spacing jittered from the seed by _hjit, never closer than the computed distance (the distance is recomputed for the jittered bearing and the jitter only lengthens it).

decisions.summary: A homestead's footprint for the minimum distance is its envelope plus its reserved woodlot seats plus, to the south, its yard's far edge plus SUN_CORRIDOR_FT; the new house's own reach is the FIRST house's footprint
decisions.why: FR-003 lists five inputs and three sun rules; the plan's footprint carries the house, yard, gardens, woodlot share and the yard's sun corridor (and so the grove-south strip, 39 ft > 22 px at 1 ft/px) but drops 'its path out' entirely - GROW_GAP is 6 px, under a corridor's 14 ft strip - and never computes the garden-shade rule. The path out is the term the GM approved by name ('a footprint that includes house, yard, garden, woodlot and the path out') and it is purpose-bearing: feature 306 R3's unfair test offered seats exactly where a neighbor's door path lay. A standing house's reserved path is known when its neighbors are offered, so including it is possible; none of the three grounds for an exception holds. Also: the next household's size is its lot's rung (known at seat order), so proxying its reach by house 0's can offer closer than FR-003's distance where house 0 is smaller - FR-004's 'never closer' needs the household's own reach or a proxy shown to be the largest.

decisions.summary: Seats offered nearest the seat center first, within FORM_BOUND times the 162 ft band's diagonal; each judged by try_place
decisions.why: The spec's edge case holds growth inside the band; FR-006's full rules decide each seat.

decisions.summary: When the heap runs dry, every standing house offers again at wider GROW_LEVELS (8 dirs ring 1; 12 dirs rings 1, 1.5; 16 dirs rings 1.25, 1.75, 2); past the last level the margin is reported short
decisions.why: Every seat is still anchored on a standing house at a multiple >= 1 of the footprint distance, so it is FR-004 growth, not the free grid; the offer count is bounded by houses x directions x rings, and running past the last level reports the margin short as FR-007 says. Not the exhaustive pass smuggled back.

decisions.summary: Jitter, gap and rings labeled guesses with reasons at the constants; placement order a map drawing convention

Front row, lattice ranks and exhaustive pass with rescue removed for settlement_form == nucleated, grow_the_margin in their place; dispersed keeps them, linear's seat_rows untouched; seat_search records grow keys
decisions.why: FR-007 literally for the nucleated form; the dispersed and linear scope is the spec's round-1 rulings (LEGITIMATE), restated, not widened. The counters only follow the removal.

decisions.summary: Where no straight or round-the-gable corridor clears, _house_candidates yields an A*-routed corridor from a dooryard door to the tree's nearest points, pulled taut, reserved leg by leg, admitted by tree_admits; on only for the nucleated seating
decisions.why: FR-005: the path is laid as the house is placed, ending on the access tree, which holds every standing house's path; the request asked for each house's path 'laid back to its neighbor's as it goes' and says nothing of straightness. Straight candidates are still tried first.

decisions.summary: The routed corridor's legs are judged by house_clear, fixtures_clear, parts_clear, standing_ground, lawful_leg, doubles_back and tree_admits - stated as 'the same tests a straight corridor passes'
decisions.why: A straight or gable candidate is also asked leaves_its_yard (access.py _house_candidates, feature 287 M8); the list omits it and the A* grid keeps off the house's own box but not its yard. FR-005 ('the placer's own corridor rules still judge it') and FR-006 ('no rule is relaxed or skipped') leave no room for a corridor rule the routed path skips. One clause fixes it: the routed candidate passes leaves_its_yard as the others do.

decisions.summary: At most 5 legs, a 12 px grid within 320 px of each door, A* weight 1.5
decisions.why: Search breadth; a seat with no route found is refused as a seat with no straight corridor is today. No rule changes.

decisions.summary: Routing classed a map drawing convention, recorded at the module docstring, indexed via _reach_index, FreeGround and the wood grid
decisions.why: Recording and indexing, as the project rules require.

decisions.summary: Dispersed and linear unchanged; only the nucleated form grows
decisions.why: The spec's round-1 rulings, unchanged in scope.

decisions.summary: Verification: prototype legs (R6), then Inashiro, pool and cohort against a detached-worktree baseline, then make done and the bookends
decisions.why: Follows FR-001 and FR-008, provided the GO verdict (R7 pending) is recorded before the first engine edit.
